Weekly rankings

Half-PPR projections if active, with realistic ranges. Tap a player for season stats.

How to read
Projection assumes the player is active (NFL availability is yes/no, so injured players show an Inactive% instead of a discount). The range bar comes from how past projections of this size actually turned out: thin line = floor to ceiling (10th to 90th percentile), thick bar = the likely middle half, tick = projection. Matchup: grade A-F ranks this week's matchups at the position; the pill is fantasy points this defense adds or removes vs an average one. TD donut: ring segments = chance of 0 / 1 / 2 / 3+ touchdowns (darker = more), center = chance of at least one. ECR is the FantasyPros expert consensus rank (faded "lw" = last week's, until Friday). A yellow edge marks a projection boosted by a teammate's absence.
Preset
Points per stat
League (sets the tiers)

Projections are stat lines, so any scoring re-scores them exactly. Blended-in expert ranks and the floor/ceiling ranges are scaled by the same ratio (an approximation). Saved on this device.

# ECR Player Projection Actual Matchup Inactive FP/G Tier Expected line Takeaway

Matchups

Model lines next to Vegas. Highlighted edges are where they disagree most.

How to read
Model lines come only from opponent-adjusted team ratings (no Vegas inputs), so a disagreement is a genuine second opinion. Spreads use betting notation (favorite minus points). Edges appear when the model differs from Vegas by 1+ point on the spread or 1.5+ on the total, and are highlighted at 3.0+ / 4.0+. Who wins each battle: every bar is a tug of war in the two teams' colors, away team always on the left and home team on the right. Whoever pushes past the middle line wins, and the number on the winner's side is how many points that edge is worth this game compared with an average matchup. Overall (top) is the model's margin. Below it, each offense against the other defense: its total is roughly how far above or below average that offense should score. Tap a matchup to split it into passing and running (the per-play edge times that offense's projected dropbacks or runs, so a run edge is never read as equal to a pass edge of the same per-play size). Everything adds up exactly: Overall = both offense-vs-defense matchups + special teams + home field and pace (projected play volume and pass/run mix). The split follows the model's own points formula, so every bar is on the same scale as the model line. Rank chips are each unit's league rank from the Power tab (green top 8, red bottom 8). Hover a row for the per-play numbers.

Power rankings

Opponent-adjusted points per game vs an average team. Everything adds up: Offense = Pass O + Run O, Defense = Pass D + Run D, Net = Offense + Defense + ST.

How to read
Every number is points per game against an average opponent: each unit's per-play rating times a league-average number of those plays (about 38 dropbacks, 25 runs and 11 special-teams plays), so the columns add up and a run edge is never read as equal to a pass edge. Hover any unit for its per-play rating. Pass O includes the team's current starting quarterback. Higher is better everywhere, including defense. Rank range is the 10th-90th percentile rank when ratings are resampled within their uncertainty (200 bootstrap resamples of games): a narrow range means the data has settled, a wide one means a few more games could move the team a lot. Colored badges are league ranks (green = top 8, red = bottom 8). Schedule: points per game the opponents took away (played) or would take away (left), unit by unit: the team's actual dropbacks against each opponent's pass defense and runs against its run defense, plus the offenses its defense faced. Positive = tougher than average; 1st = hardest. Re-scored every week with current ratings. Arrows show the move since last week.
